validation.typecheck: passed: compiler, tests and all examples

change: Add synchronous stringifyJson, typed parseJson<T> and global JSON.stringify compiler intrinsics. Serialization uses native JSON encoding; parsing uses an internal dictionary envelope and extracts the value, supporting scalar/object/flat-array roots.

verifiedShortcut.name: TS-JSON-Conversion
verifiedShortcut.completion: All eight expected results appeared in order. After the final Done, the editor showed play available with no error.
verifiedShortcut.importComparison: All 148 imported actions read from the simulator database match the compiled output exactly.

nativeCoverage: Typed object parsing and boolean condition
Round trip of composed objects with a singleton array field
Empty, singleton and multi-item root arrays
Text with quotes, backslash, newline and emoji; empty string serialization
Boolean and negative fractional number roots
A singleton array of objects preserves its array shape and typed fields
compilerCoverage: Argument evaluation once, including effects when conversion results are ignored
Composition with synchronous helpers, array callbacks and await
Lexical/import shadowing of JSON and renamed intrinsic imports
Parser receives a materialized text attachment and exposes the extracted value
Reject missing types, invalid input categories, null/nullable root types, opaque content, matrices and unsupported JSON options
All prior native fixtures retain their expectations; the new fixture raw/catalog roundtrips pass
investigations: A native detect.dictionary probe with plain parameter strings produced no useful parsed object; a materialized text attachment parsed the object correctly.
A directly parsed root numeric array did not produce usable array values. The final dictionary-envelope implementation was verified for arrays and scalars.
limitations: parseJson<T> expects valid JSON and declares the result shape without runtime schema validation.
Malformed input follows native parser behavior; strict JavaScript syntax-error semantics are not promised.
Root null/undefined, opaque output types and arrays of arrays are unsupported.
No replacer/reviver, indentation, toJSON callbacks or untyped global JSON.parse.
Native key ordering, finite-number precision and JSON-compatible input requirements apply.
Physical devices, other OS versions and full Shortcuts/TypeScript coverage remain unverified.
